subject: physics
title: Simple Harmonic Motion Basics
welcome_lead: Meet a = -ω² x, the defining equation of every oscillator from springs to atoms.
meta_desc: A-Level Further Mechanics adventure on SHM definition, equations and period.
final_note: If acceleration is opposite and proportional to displacement, you have SHM.

concepts.def: Motion with a = -ω² x; restoring force ∝ displacement.
Position in the cycle, measured as angle.

walkthroughs.body_html: SHM is defined by acceleration directly proportional to displacement and pointing back to equilibrium. The negative sign is essential — it's a restoring acceleration.
Starting at the maximum, x(t) = A cos(ω t). Then v = -A ω sin(ω t) and a = -A ω² cos(ω t) = -ω² x. Maximum speed v_max = A ω.
Spring of stiffness k: T = 2π √(m/k). Simple pendulum: T = 2π √(L/g). Both independent of amplitude (small angles only).

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.

mcqs.q: What force keeps a car moving in a circle around a bend?
options: The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.
Friction from the road acting towards the centre of the circle — centripetal force.
The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
A centrifugal force pushes the car outwards from the centre.

mcqs.q: For a projectile launched horizontally, what affects the horizontal component of velocity during flight (ignoring air resistance)?
options: The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
Nothing — horizontal velocity stays constant; only vertical velocity changes due to gravity.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Gravity slows down both the vertical and horizontal motion.
